clue.text: Suppress start of spillage above dam

indicators.note: in a down entry one piece sits above the next, so this places the letter first
the start of the word spillage is its opening letter only

parts.note: a dam is the mother of an animal, especially a horse

explanation.surface: Instructions for stopping a spill from overflowing a dam.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dam' looks like a barrier for water, but here it is a livestock word for a mother.
explanation.definitionFit: To smother something is to stifle or suppress it, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Show little interest in what Miles Davis used to do with his trumpet

definitions.meaning: to act nonchalant and unbothered, keeping one's feelings hidden

definitions.text: what Miles Davis used to do with his trumpet
definitions.meaning: Miles Davis was a pioneer of cool jazz, so he literally performed in that style

explanation.surface: A remark about appearing indifferent, set beside the jazz trumpeter Miles Davis.
explanation.walkthrough: Miles Davis's album Birth of the Cool helped launch the 'cool jazz' style, so the phrase works literally of his playing.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means acting calm and unconcerned; in jazz it means performing in the cool style.

clue.text: See 2
At present no amount of money over a year covers salary cap

indicators.note: in a down entry, a piece over another comes before it
in a down entry the piece that covers another sits on top of it, so comes first

parts.note: taken as written
a wad is a thick roll of banknotes

indicators.note: the cap of a word is its top, which in a down entry means the first letter

explanation.surface: A complaint that these days no pay packet over a year can cover a capped salary.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Over' and 'covers' are both positional in this down clue: each puts the following piece below the one before.
explanation.definitionFit: Nowadays means in the present time, so it matches the phrase at present.

clue.text: Being all fingers and thumbs it's the job for her

definitions.text: Being all fingers and thumbs it's the job for her

parts.words: Being all fingers and thumbs it's the job for her
parts.note: all fingers and thumbs usually means clumsy, but here it describes a job that deals entirely with hands and nails

explanation.surface: A clumsy woman being steered towards a suitable career.
explanation.walkthrough: The idiom 'all fingers and thumbs' means clumsy, which would be a poor fit for most jobs; read literally it describes someone who works only on hands.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who tends and shapes fingernails spends the working day dealing with fingers and thumbs.

clue.text: Ice mass beginning to get more flimsy

indicators.note: the beginning of the word get is its first letter

parts.note: lacier means more lacy, finer and more delicate

explanation.surface: Ice that starts to thin and get flimsier.
explanation.definitionFit: A glacier is a huge slow-moving body of ice, so an ice mass describes it.

clue.text: Hull bird confronts former rival

indicators.note: confronts means faces, so the bird stands in front of the other piece

parts.note: Rod Hull was a British TV entertainer whose act centred on a puppet emu
late means former, as in the late chairman

explanation.surface: A bird from the city of Hull squaring up to an old enemy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hull' suggests the English city, but it is Rod Hull, a 1970s-80s British comic famous for his aggressive puppet Emu.
explanation.definitionFit: To emulate someone is to try to equal or rival them, a verb synonym.

clue.text: 'In Particular' — a Blyton novel

indicators.note: novel as an adjective means new, so these letters take a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A book title for an Enid Blyton story called In Particular.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Novel' reads as a book by Enid Blyton, the British children's author, but it is the signal to rearrange A BLYTON.
explanation.definitionFit: Notably and in particular both single out something as especially worth mentioning.

clue.text: Triesman originally probing feigning and provocation

indicators.note: something probing is pushed inside, so this letter goes into the other piece

parts.note: simulation is pretence or feigning

indicators.note: originally points to the first letter of the word Triesman

explanation.surface: A man named Triesman first poking at pretence and provocation.
explanation.definitionFit: Stimulation is rousing or arousing, close to provocation as a stirring-up.

clue.text: With toasty fare dished up it's a tempting invitation

indicators.note: food that is dished up is served out, so the letters are laid out anew

explanation.surface: Toasted food served as a lure to make guests linger.
explanation.definitionFit: Asking someone to remain for an afternoon meal is a tempting offer to linger.

clue.text: Have a strong desire to thumb a lift down the Old Kent Road?

indicators.note: the Old Kent Road is in working-class south London, where Cockney speech drops the opening H

parts.note: to hitch is to hitchhike by thumbing a lift

explanation.surface: Wanting badly to hitchhike along a famous London street.
explanation.walkthrough: The Old Kent Road is a street in south-east London; Cockney accent drops initial H, so 'itch' is how a local would say the word.
explanation.definitionFit: To itch for something is to long for it, an idiomatic sense of craving.

clue.text: Kinky nude lump is a regular swinger

indicators.note: kinky means twisted, so these letters get twisted into a new order

explanation.surface: A risqué image of a naked lump who swings regularly.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a swingers' party; the swinging is a clock weight's regular motion.
explanation.definitionFit: A clock's weighted rod swings back and forth at a steady rate, so it is a regular swinger.

clue.text: Haunt where French and English troops get time for unwinding

indicators.note: get here joins the pieces, the troops acquiring the next piece after them

parts.note: a den is a favourite haunt or hideaway
ou is French for where
men are soldiers, troops

explanation.surface: A hangout where French and English soldiers find time to relax.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unwinding' suggests relaxing, but it means the untying of a plot's knots.
explanation.definitionFit: The French word for a story's final resolution literally means an untying or unknotting.

clue.text: Combined with energy an overall sharpness

indicators.note: an overall is worn over everything, so these two letters wrap round the rest

parts.note: cum means together with, as in study-cum-bedroom
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: Sharpness and energy together give a general keenness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Overall' looks like 'in total' but tells A and N to sit outside CUM and E.
explanation.definitionFit: Acumen is shrewdness or keenness of mind, a figurative sharpness.

clue.text: Heads of romaine lettuce are tastefully scattered in nouvelle cuisine that's impracticable

indicators.note: the letters are scattered through a new version of the next word, nouvelle being French for new
the heads of these four words are their first letters

explanation.surface: A recipe note about scattering lettuce leaves elegantly in a nouvelle cuisine dish.
explanation.walkthrough: RLAT, the first letters, mixed in with the letters of CUISINE, rearranged as 'nouvelle' (new) demands.
explanation.definitionFit: Something unrealistic cannot be achieved in practice, so it is impracticable.

clue.text: European Union record is initially embarrassing to praise

parts.note: a log is a written record, as in a ship's log
taken as written

indicators.note: initially points to the first letter of embarrassing

explanation.surface: Praise from the European Union recorded as initially awkward.
explanation.definitionFit: To eulogise is to praise highly, especially in a formal tribute.

clue.text: Brussels ruled out of euphemism for birthplace of rock'n'roll

indicators.note: these letters are excluded and what is left out of the long word is rearranged

parts.note: Brussels is the seat of the European Union, so it stands for EU

explanation.surface: Brussels banning euphemisms in a note about the home of rock music.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Brussels ruled out of' removes EU from EUPHEMISM, leaving PHEMISM to be rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Memphis, Tennessee, home of Sun Studio and Elvis's early records, is often called rock and roll's birthplace.

clue.text: Peer got special ward

indicators.note: special suggests something altered or made different, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A lord who obtained a private hospital room.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ward' suggests a hospital, but it is a person under someone's protection.
explanation.definitionFit: A protégé is someone guided and protected by a patron, as a ward is by a guardian.

clue.text: Part 2: Paraphrase 'quelque part'

indicators.note: part of the words is taken, so the answer lies within them

explanation.surface: A French exercise: put 'quelque part' into other words.
explanation.walkthrough: The run starts at the end of 'Paraphrase' and continues into 'quelque'; 'quelque part' is French for 'somewhere'.
explanation.definitionFit: A sequel is the follow-up work, the second part of a story.

clue.text: Reluctant to say anything after disastrous Act I's performance

indicators.note: a disastrous act has gone badly wrong, so these letters are jumbled

parts.note: the possessive 's adds no letter, leaving the words act and I
a turn is a short stage performance

explanation.surface: Struck dumb after a dreadful first act.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Disastrous' is the anagram signal for ACT I alone; the possessive gives no S, which a solver may wrongly include. 'After' only links definition to wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A taciturn person habitually says very little, unwilling to talk.

clue.text: Captain Fantastic not one for sleep

indicators.note: fantastic means wild or fanciful, so the letters are rearranged, once one is taken away

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A great captain who is not one for sleeping.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not one' removes I from the letters of CAPTAIN before they are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: A catnap is a short light sleep or doze.

clue.text: Plans reviewed for junk mail

indicators.note: reviewed read as re-viewed, looked at from the other end, so the word goes backwards

parts.note: maps are plans or charts

explanation.surface: Plans looked over again and dismissed as junk mail.
explanation.definitionFit: Spam is unwanted bulk mail, especially electronic.

clue.text: Others twig rewording is to make the illiterate appear literate

definitions.text: to make the illiterate appear literate

indicators.note: rewording means changing the words, so these letters are put in a new order

explanation.surface: Other people catching on that rewording makes an uneducated writer look polished.
explanation.definitionFit: A hired writer produces text for someone else to sign, making a poor writer seem accomplished.

clue.text: Complaints with no case ready for action

indicators.note: the case of a word is its outer shell, so its first and last letters are dropped

parts.note: gripes are grumbles or complaints

explanation.surface: Grievances with no legal case, yet ripe for action.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Case' sounds legal, but here it is the word's outside letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Ripe means mature and ready, as a situation ripe for change.

clue.text: A pint is ordered for musician

indicators.note: ordered means arranged, so these letters are put in a new order

explanation.surface: A drink being ordered for a performer at the bar.
explanation.definitionFit: A pianist is a musician who plays the piano.

clue.text: Rush about wildly and crash into messenger

parts.note: to ram is to crash into something
a page is a young messenger or attendant

explanation.surface: Charging around and colliding with a courier.
explanation.definitionFit: To rampage is to charge about in a wild or violent manner.
